text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.
- Pensioners to start receiving debts from pension fund from March 1. Minimum monthly rate will be 50 kuna.
- Foreign Minister Mate Granic visits Belgrade on Wednesday to discuss final steps in returning Serb enclave Eastern Slavonia to Zagreb rule's and establishing border regime with Serbia.
- Maslenica bridge linking Pag island with the Adriatic coast, which was damaged by war, should reopen for traffic by the beginning of March.

- Some 600,000 German tourists expected to spend holidays on the Adriatic coast this year, Croatian Tourist Associatiaon says at fair in Munich. Reports from Salzburg announce a great comeback of Austrian tourists to Croatia as well.
- Croatian Railways (HZ) cancelled over 50 trains in the past four days because of fuel shortage. Fuel supplier, oil company INA, says HZ owes them 40 million kuna.
- Three teenagers from the coastal town Zadar, surfing Internet, broke into Pentagon's information system causing $2,500 damage. Police are investigating.
- Bank rehabilitation agency has written off debts of state companies to Privredna Banka Zagreb as part of its overhaul. The bank has no more liquidity problems, says its acting director Ivan Tesija.
- Beginner judges cannot solve commercial disputes, says law faculty dean Jaksa Barbic.
- Splitska Banka regains clients' trust and reports increase in savings since the overhaul which started last April. The bank now faces restructuring process.
- Commentary: Total jobless might hit 300,000 this year, judging by last year's increase of 8.5 percent.
- Dubrovnik to host an international festival of tourist marketing, says its director Neeraj Nayar. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
